news.content_snippet:
Microsoft AI (MAI) is targeting always-on AI agents with new models for code, security, images, speech, and routing. The main yardstick is the lineup of its own partner, OpenAI.

At its Ignite conference, MAI unveiled seven new models, releasing them in a single batch rather than spread across the year, just as it did at Build in June. Microsoft is positioning the new lineup primarily on price-to-performance. The company cites rapidly rising token spending among customers that want to run AI age
news.summary_en: Microsoft AI unveiled seven in-house models at Ignite to replace third-party models across its product suite, including GitHub Copilot and Microsoft 365. The primary driver is to mitigate surging costs from continuous AI agent tasks, with Microsoft claiming superior price-to-performance ratios compared to existing OpenAI and Anthropic offerings.
news.article_content_en:
Microsoft AI (MAI) is targeting always-on AI agents with new models for code, security, images, speech, and routing. The main yardstick is the lineup of its own partner, OpenAI.

At its Ignite conference, MAI unveiled seven new models, releasing them in a single batch rather than spread across the year, just as it did at Build in June. Microsoft is positioning the new lineup primarily on price-to-performance. The company cites rapidly rising token spending among customers that want to run AI agents around the clock. Its code models target everyday enterprise coding tasks and aren't yet optimized for harder work such as foundational research or long-horizon agentic workflows, Microsoft says.

### MAI Code 2 approaches GPT-6.1 Sol and Opus 5.5 at a promotional price

According to Microsoft, MAI Code 2 averages 98 percent of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance across four benchmarks at 40 percent of the cost. Against Claude Opus 5.5, it reaches 96 percent of the performance at 5 percent of the cost. Microsoft tested on DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal Bench 2.1, SWE-Atlas, and FrontierCode v1.1. Three of the tests ran on Microsoft's internal MSBench platform using the GitHub Copilot CLI without sub-agents. Microsoft is calculating a 50 percent promotional discount for its own model.

In blind comparisons of frontend work such as UIs, games, data visualizations, and SVG graphics, human evaluators preferred MAI Code 2's output 64 percent of the time over GPT-6 Sol, Microsoft says.

The successor to MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, MAI Code 2 Flash, is designed for code explanations, targeted edits, and routine fixes. It's said to match GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at 65 and 20 percent of their respective costs.

Microsoft derived MAI Work Flash from the Flash model. It runs in Microsoft 365 and Fabric IQ. On internal Excel and PowerPoint benchmarks, it matches GPT-6 Luna, Microsoft says. In Word, it performs similarly to GPT-6.1 Sol while consuming about 42 percent fewer input tokens. For generating DAX queries in Power BI, it outperforms GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Opus 5.5.

In GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 costs $0.50 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens at the promotional price through May 17, 2027, then $1 and $5. MAI Code 2 Flash costs $0.05 and $0.25 until then, rising to $0.10 and $0.50.

### Security model with a cleaned-up benchmark

MAI Cyber 2 Flash solves 92.3 percent of the tasks in the CyberGym-E2E vulnerability benchmark, Microsoft says. GPT-6 Astra reaches 91.5 percent but needs twice the reasoning budget. Per task, the MAI model costs less than 2 percent of GPT-6 Astra, with per-token costs at one hundredth. On WebExploitBench, it scores 40.4 percent, ahead of GPT-5.6 Cyber at 38.4 percent.

During evaluation, Microsoft found that 10 percent of the roughly 900 CyberGym tasks draw on the same open-source projects and vulnerability reports as parts of its own training data. The reference solutions never entered training, the company says. Microsoft removed those tasks for all models anyway and scored only the rest.

A comparison with GPT-6 Cyber is missing so far. The model is available only to selected customers. Agentic benchmarks with tools still need extra safety measures, Microsoft says. The company plans to publish those results in the coming weeks.

The context window spans one million tokens, four times the size of MAI Cyber 1.1 Flash. Output tokens cost 86 percent less than the predecessor's. MAI Cyber models already handle nearly 40 percent of scans on Microsoft's security platform MDASH, the press release states.

Microsoft lists MAI Cyber 2 Flash at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, compared with $10 and $50 for GPT-6 Astra. On CyberGym-E2E, that works out to $0.45 per task instead of $34.38.

### Microsoft's decision model now runs on Google's Gemma

Microsoft-Decision-1.1 handles routing, classification, prioritization, and workflow control. The model picks from developer-approved actions and returns calibrated confidence scores. When uncertainty is high, apps can escalate instead of acting on a wrong decision. If information is incomplete, the model is designed to abstain.

Its foundation is Google's mixture-of-experts model Gemma 4 26B A4B. The predecessor was built on Qwen3.5-9B. Microsoft trained the new model with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning on hundreds of synthetic and licensed datasets and runs it on a proprietary inference engine.

On the Decision Index v2.1 from Artificial Analysis, Decision 1.1 scores 68 points. That's six more than its predecessor and above Jev 1.14, Gemini Decision 1, and GPT-6 Luna (Decisions). Microsoft also tested it on 102 internal benchmarks with more than 385,000 questions, where it achieves the highest average accuracy among eight decision models.

The model now accepts images, including screenshots. In Copilot, it decides whether a request goes to Copilot or Cowork. It performs as accurately as a large language model but 2.2 times faster and 4.4 times cheaper, Microsoft says. In Cowork, its Auto function controls how much reasoning effort a task receives.

Microsoft charges $0.042 per million input tokens, or $0.05 in the EU data zone. Output tokens are free.

Another specialized model appears in the Book of News for Ignite. Microsoft-Retriever-1 gathers relevant information from enterprise documents for agents in Foundry IQ. Instead of running a single search, the model plans its queries, evaluates the results, and issues follow-ups until it has enough material for a well-grounded answer. Microsoft says that's faster and more efficient than previous methods. Retriever-1 launches as a preview. The Model Router in Foundry now also selects automatically from an expanded pool of models.

### Image editing just ahead of OpenAI

MAI Image 2.7 leads the Artificial Analysis image-editing leaderboard with 1,215 Elo points from 5,478 votes. It's four points ahead of GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst (max) at one-fifth the cost. For text-to-image generation, the model ranks fourth on that leaderboard. MAI Image 2.7 costs about $35 per 1,000 images. Flash costs about $10.

The model can change the color, material, or position of individual objects without altering the rest of the image. It also generates transparent backgrounds. The smaller Flash variant costs less than a third and powers Canvas, a new image editor in MAI Labs. MAI Image has been the default model in Bing Image Creator since June. Adobe, Figma Weave, Minute (Sports Illustrated), Wirestock, and Manus work with MAI Image, Microsoft says.

### Speech model compatible with OpenAI's API

MAI Realtime 1 is Microsoft's first speech-to-speech model. It's designed to handle interruptions, wait until speakers finish, and recognize requests even with background noise. For harder tasks, it falls back to a more powerful reasoning engine billed per token. The base rate is charged per audio minute. On Big Bench Audio, τ-Voice, and tests with Dynamics 365, it outperforms GPT Realtime 2.1, Microsoft says.

Because it's compatible with the OpenAI Realtime API, existing voice apps can switch over easily. Agoda and Reservations.ai are testing the model. Microsoft also plans to bring it to the Dynamics 365 Contact Center and Dragon Copilot, where nurses would use it to practice patient conversations.

Dragon Copilot Transcribe, based on MAI Transcribe 2, now handles all doctor-patient transcriptions in Dragon Copilot. That amounts to 10 million conversations per month, Microsoft says. In multilingual workflows, the error rate drops by half. For its own large models, Microsoft now uses the Maia 200 chip, the second generation of its AI accelerator, said to deliver 1.7 times more tokens per watt.

Microsoft charges one US cent per audio minute. Reasoning costs an extra $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens.

### Licensed weights available only through the Microsoft account team

With MAI Licensed Weights, companies can fine-tune MAI models with their own data and run them in their own Azure environment. Data and customizations stay with the customer. Microsoft says it will use them for training its own models only with explicit consent.

The company positions the offering as an alternative to open weights, whose provenance and behavior are hard for enterprises to verify. One example is US carrier AT&T, where a customized model for 5G network operations analysis reportedly outperformed GPT-6.1 Sol on standard tasks at roughly one-fiftieth of the cost. A launch date and pricing are still pending. Interested companies should contact their Microsoft account team. The offering is set to arrive "shortly"through Microsoft's Frontier Company program.

MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash are available in GitHub Copilot, with Code 2 Flash also in a limited preview in Foundry. OpenRouter, Vercel, Hermes, Open Code, and Kilo are expected to follow. MAI Image 2.7 and Flash are in public preview in Foundry and on fal, Genspark, OpenRouter, and Vercel. Decision 1.1 is generally available in Foundry, on OpenRouter, and through Vercel's AI Gateway. MAI Realtime 1 can be tried in MAI Labs and is available as a Foundry preview, free until the public preview launches. MAI Cyber 2 Flash is exclusive to Microsoft's security products. In MDASH, it will automatically replace the existing model in the MAI profile for eligible customers starting mid-December.

In April, Microsoft and OpenAI restructured their partnership. OpenAI can now sell its products through any cloud provider, but Azure remains the primary cloud partner. Microsoft holds a non-exclusive license to OpenAI's models and products through 2032.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Imagine having an AI Agent that can do more than answer questions.

With @meetmotes, the idea is to connect each Genesis NFT to a dedicated Agent and Smart Account, giving it a defined environment to work within.

But what does user control actually look like?

Imagine funding an Agent with 1,000 USDC to manage an approved list of DeFi assets.

You could set:
→ Maximum 10% per trade
→ A daily spending cap of 300 USDC
→ Slippage limit of 0.5%
→ Borrowing disabled
→ Pause new trades if the account value falls to 850 USDC

The Agent can research and propose actions, but transactions must pass the account's policy checks before execution.

That's the important distinction: AI can make decisions, but permissions should determine what it is allowed to do.

Motes' documentation describes this architecture, including policy enforcement, execution logs, pause controls and permission revocation.

What I still want to see is the evidence in practice:

→ Verified smart-account contracts and independent security reviews
→ Onchain records showing limits enforced on every transaction
→ Execution logs covering successful, rejected and failed actions
→ A tested pause and revocation process

The concept behind $MOTES is interesting, but reliable execution and genuine owner control need to be demonstrated, not just promised.

More research to come.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
想象一下，有一个人工智能代理不仅可以回答问题。

通过 @meetmotes，其想法是将每个 Genesis NFT 连接到专用代理和智能帐户，为其提供一个定义的工作环境。

但用户控件实际上是什么样子的呢？

想象一下，用 1,000 USDC 资助一名代理来管理经过批准的 DeFi 资产列表。

您可以设置：
→ 每笔交易最高 10%
→ 每日支出上限为 300 USDC
→ 滑点限制为 0.5%
→ 禁止借贷
→ 如果账户价值跌至 850 USDC，则暂停新交易

代理可以研究并提出行动建议，但交易在执行之前必须通过账户的策略检查。

这是重要的区别：人工智能可以做出决定，但权限应该决定它可以做什么。

Motes 的文档描述了这种架构，包括策略实施、执行日志、暂停控制和权限撤销。

我还想看到的是实践中的证据：

→ 经过验证的智能账户合约和独立的安全审查
→ 链上记录显示每笔交易的限制
→ 执行日志涵盖成功、拒绝和失败的操作
→ 经过测试的暂停和撤销流程

$MOTES 背后的概念很有趣，但需要证明可靠的执行和真正的所有者控制，而不仅仅是承诺。

更多研究即将到来。

→ 经过验证的智能账户合约和独立的安全审查

→ 执行日志涵盖成功、拒绝和失败的操作
→ 经过测试的暂停和撤销流程

$MOTES 背后的概念很有趣，但需要证明可靠的执行和真正的所有者控制，而不仅仅是承诺。

更多研究即将到来。

The existential risk for enterp
celebrity.title_zh:
@ypatil125 @rythmrg @lindensli 期待您来到 Palo Alto Networks。

企业公司的生存风险是缺乏前沿人才，以及有人利用人工智能重塑我们业务的可能性。因此，新团队的首要任务是确保 Palo Alto
celebrity.full_text_en:
@ypatil125 @rythmrg @lindensli looking forward to welcoming you to Palo Alto Networks. 

The existential risk for enterprise companies is their lack of frontier level talent and the possiblity that someone reinvents our business with AI. So first and foremost the new team has a task, to ensure Palo Alto Networks is the world leader in applying frontier AI to its security portfolio and I can't think of a better person to help drive that  @ypatil125 as Co-Chief AI Officer I expect him and his team to help us transform to an AI first company. I have always maintained winning teams are humble enough to know what they can do and when they need to bring in a team to lead with them. We will be stronger and better together. 

I firmly believe that the acceleration of enterprise AI adoption will be driven by a reliable, scalable, secure implementation of open weight/source models. Upon inspection, there is not many scale players who are ready to serve this markets from ideation with customers, to training, continuous learning and partnering with secure inference providers.We think we can help the  Applied Compute team with our enterprise capabilities and deliver on this vision together. 

Lastly and equally important I believe- to provide true reliability, explanability and verifiability of AI in enterprise applications - we should be training a digital twin or "supervisory AI" which is reward hacked to observe "task AI" and alert on non compliance. It is impossible to deliver safety and security without training both models together with different objective functions. Without being able to interrogate chain of thought, we intend to work with the Applied Compute team to validate this future .

We intend to become a key player in the AI economy in engendering trust in AI so we can collectively drive Enterprise trust. 

Yes, there will be things to learn, pivot and adapt as we continue on this journey, but me and the team are excited to go after this with the @appliedcompute team. 

In times of technology inflection, if you don't act on your instinct - you lose.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
@ypatil125 @rythmrg @lindensli 期待您来到 Palo Alto Networks。

企业公司的生存风险是缺乏前沿人才，以及有人利用人工智能重塑我们业务的可能性。因此，新团队的首要任务是确保 Palo Alto Networks 在将前沿人工智能应用到其安全产品组合方面处于世界领先地位，我想不出比这更好的人选了。@ypatil125 作为联合首席人工智能官，我希望他和他的团队能够帮助我们转型为人工智能优先的公司。我一直认为获胜的团队足够谦虚，知道自己能做什么，以及何时需要引入团队来领导他们。我们将一起变得更强、更好。

我坚信，开放权重/源代码模型的可靠、可扩展、安全实施将推动企业人工智能的加速采用。经过检查，没有多少规模参与者准备好服务这个市场，从与客户的构思，到培训、持续学习以及与安全推理提供商的合作。我们认为我们可以利用我们的企业能力帮助应用计算团队并共同实现这一愿景。

最后，我认为同样重要的是，为了在企业应用程序中提供人工智能的真正可靠性、可解释性和可验证性，我们应该训练一个数字孪生或“监督人工智能”，它会被奖励黑客观察“任务人工智能”并对不合规情况发出警报。如果不使用不同的目标函数对两个模型进行训练，就不可能提供安全性。在无法询问思想链的情况下，我们打算与应用计算团队合作来验证这个未来。

我们打算成为人工智能经济中建立人工智能信任的关键参与者，以便我们能够共同推动企业信任。

是的，随着我们继续这一旅程，将会有一些东西需要学习、调整和适应，但我和团队很高兴能与 @appliedcompute 团队一起追求这一目标。

在技​​术变革的时代，如果你不按照自己的直觉行事，你就会失败。

又一个经典的人性泡芙作品。收据如下。

从表面上看，她在《纽约时报》上对 Anthropic
celebrity.full_text_en:
The New York Times just ran Anthropic's best ad of the IPO. They call it a profile. It reads like a prospectus. The author left out who funded her reporting.

Another classic Anthropic puff piece. Receipts below.

On the surface, her pre-IPO profile of Anthropic in the New York Times lands a few soft, harmless jabs. Strip away the Silicon Valley jargon, though, and every "critique" turns into a high-end sales pitch aimed straight at "Americans' retirement portfolios." That's you.

Here are the receipts she printed, and the one she hid.

1. The "reluctant hero" trick.

After paragraphs of employees agonizing over how to "slow down A.I.," the piece admits Anthropic's #1 priority with IPO cash is buying massive compute to reach "recursive self-improvement" (AI building uncontrollable AI) before OpenAI and China.

Meanwhile, it warns about mass layoffs while being the leading seller of the AI agents that "threaten to replace white-collar workers."

It sells the flood and the sandbags.

2. The $70 billion fund, and the fine print.

The company is putting 5% of a $1.4T company ($70 billion) into a "Public Benefit Fund" for donations of its choosing. Its employees are pledging their stock to charity too.

Read her order: animal welfare, global health, AI safety. Then, last: "Many have begun giving big to political campaigns."

Charity on the label. Politics in the fine print.

Tucked between the "ascetic monk" anecdotes is the real pitch: insiders aren't selling, Claude Code "reinvented" coding, and revenue passed OpenAI.

That isn't a profile. That's a prospectus with a byline.

3. The monopoly free pass.

Anthropic is lobbying Congress for an antitrust exemption (a legal cartel), pre-empting state AI laws, and talking about becoming "more powerful than the government."

A five-tier stock structure: you buy the shares, they keep the vote.

Count the named critics in the entire piece: zero.

Even after citing examples of Claude "only pretending to follow its instructions," how does Sun let it off the hook? One magic sentence:

"I do not doubt these good intentions."

Compare how she treats regular Americans. In August, she toured the Midwest towns fighting AI data centers on their land, then filed their anger under: "'AI populism' is more about populism than about AI."

A Wisconsin town fights a data center: populism.
A trillion-dollar AI lab sells its IPO: good intentions.

The neighbors get diagnosed. The billionaires get believed.

4. The missing receipt.

The biggest conflict isn't in Anthropic's prospectus. It's in the byline.

The money: Sun's August data-center story ends: "This story was supported by a grant from the Tarbell Center for AI Journalism." Tarbell is bankrolled by Coefficient Giving, the foundation of Anthropic early investor Dustin Moskovitz.

The overlap: She wrote that her D.C. party overlapped with the Coefficient Giving team retreat: "The lines got blurry—I think my group was the intersection of both."

Her words. Not mine.

5. The hypocrisy.

On 80,000 Hours, she set the rule: "I don't think that you can do especially credible either journalistic work or policy advocacy work if you are employed by a lab: you are going to be seen as a shill. You are correctly seen as a shill."

Same show, when the money came from the lab's investors instead of the lab, she called that a witch hunt: they're "going after all the Tarbell fellows and saying these people are just Anthropic shills."

Lab paycheck: shill. Lab investor's grant: witch hunt.

Then she took a Tarbell grant herself. Then she wrote Anthropic's IPO profile in the New York Times. Then she left out the disclosure.

Her rule. Her money. Her silence.

In August, she could type the disclosure. In November, on the eve of Anthropic's IPO, she left it out.

So admit it.

You took money from Anthropic's investor network. Admit it.
You were in the room with the funders. Your words. Admit it.
You wrote their sales pitch on the eve of their IPO. Admit it.
You left out the one sentence you already know how to type. 
Admit it.

Regular Americans report every dollar to the IRS. 
You couldn't spare your readers one sentence.

By her own standard, what is she?

Who's the shill now?

Tarbell fellows?

celebrity.full_text_zh:
《纽约时报》刚刚刊登了 Anthropic 首次公开募股的最佳广告。他们称之为个人资料。它读起来就像招股说明书。作者没有提及谁资助了她的报道。

又一个经典的人性泡芙作品。收据如下。

从表面上看，她在《纽约时报》上对 Anthropic 进行首次公开​​募股前的介绍，受到了一些温和、无害的攻击。不过，抛开硅谷的行话，每一次“批评”都会变成直接针对“美国人的退休投资组合”的高端推销。那就是你。

这是她打印的收据和她藏起来的收据。

1.“英雄不甘”的伎俩。

在一段段员工苦苦思索如何“放慢人工智能速度”之后，这篇文章承认，Anthropic 在 IPO 现金方面的第一要务是购买大量计算资源，以在 OpenAI 和 China 之前实现“递归自我改进”（人工智能构建无法控制的人工智能）。

与此同时，该公司警告说，在成为“威胁要取代白领工人”的人工智能代理的主要销售商的同时，该公司可能会出现大规模裁员。

它出售洪水和沙袋。

2. 700 亿美元的基金和细则。

该公司将一家价值 1.4T 美元的公司（700 亿美元）的 5% 投入“公共福利基金”，用于其选择的捐赠。它的员工也将他们的股票捐献给慈善机构。

阅读她的命令：动物福利、全球健康、人工智能安全。然后，最后：“许多人已经开始大力支持政治运动。”

标签上的慈善。精美印刷中的政治。

在“苦行僧”轶事之间隐藏着真正的卖点：内部人士不出售，Claude Code“重新发明”了编码，收入超过了 OpenAI。

那不是个人资料。这是一份带有署名的招股说明书。

3.垄断免费通行证。

Anthropic 正在游说国会申请反垄断豁免（合法卡特尔），抢占各州人工智能法律的先发地位，并谈论变得“比政府更强大”。

五层股票结构：你购买股票，他们保留投票权。

算一下整篇文章中被点名的批评家：零。

即使引用了Claude“只是假装遵循其指示”的例子，Sun又如何让它摆脱困境呢？一句神奇的话：

“我并不怀疑这些善意。”

比较一下她如何对待普通美国人。八月，她巡视了中西部城镇，在他们的土地上与人工智能数据中心作斗争，然后表达了自己的愤怒：“‘人工智能民粹主义’更多的是民粹主义，而不是人工智能。”

威斯康星州的一个小镇与数据中心作斗争：民粹主义。
价值数万亿美元的人工智能实验室出售其 IPO：良好的意愿。

邻居确诊。亿万富翁们被相信了。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Thursday! A new morning, a fresh cup of coffee, and another interesting development in the AI agent space.

Something I've been paying attention to with @termix_ai is how it approaches the onboarding problem.

Building an AI agent is one thing. Giving that agent access to real opportunities and letting it participate in an economy is another challenge.

TermiX is working to make this connection simpler through its Agent Skills.

Instead of requiring developers to build an entirely new agent from scratch, they can connect existing AI agents to TermiX and let them interact with https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3.

Once connected, agents can discover services, respond to opportunities, take jobs, and participate in the on-chain settlement process.

I think this matters because adoption often depends on how easily existing tools can become part of a new ecosystem.

If developers can bring the agents they already use into a shared marketplace, TermiX doesn't have to rely only on people creating new agents specifically for its platform.

Of course, easier access also brings new responsibilities. Permissions, wallet security, transaction limits, and human oversight remain important when agents are allowed to act on our behalf.

For me, the interesting question is no longer just how smart an AI agent can become.

It's how easily that agent can connect to other services, find useful work, and create real value.

That's an important direction for the agent economy, and one worth watching as TermiX continues to evolve.

Have a productive Thursday, everyone! 🚀
celebrity.full_text_zh:
朋友们早上好！ ☀️☕

星期四快乐！新的早晨，一杯新鲜的咖啡，以及人工智能代理领域的另一个有趣的发展。

我一直关注 @termix_ai 的是它如何解决入职问题。

构建人工智能代理是一回事。让代理人获得真正的机会并让其参与经济是另一个挑战。

TermiX 正在努力通过其代理技能来简化这种连接。

他们无需要求开发人员从头开始构建全新的代理，而是可以将现有的 AI 代理连接到 TermiX，并让它们与 进行交互。

连接后，代理可以发现服务、响应机会、接受工作并参与链上结算流程。

我认为这很重要，因为采用通常取决于现有工具成为新生态系统一部分的容易程度。

如果开发人员可以将他们已经使用的代理引入共享市场，TermiX 就不必仅仅依靠人们专门为其平台创建新代理。

当然，更便捷的访问也带来了新的责任。当允许代理代表我们行事时，权限、钱包安全、交易限制和人工监督仍然很重要。

对我来说，有趣的问题不再只是人工智能代理能变得多聪明。

这是代理可以多么轻松地连接到其他服务、找到有用的工作并创造真正的价值。

这是代理经济的一个重要方向，随着 TermiX 的不断发展，值得关注。

大家周四过得充实！ 🚀

celebrity.full_text_en:
THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 together, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Opus-level judgment on every big call, without paying Opus rates for every routine turn.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes the code
→ Haiku 5.5 explores files and docs in parallel
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls
→ you stop spending Opus on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku explores. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and edits code
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5
> docs pulls the API reference on Haiku 5.5
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reads the whole transcript when consulted
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three read-only Haiku 5.5 subagents: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), docs (pulls the API reference).
3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before locking a plan, after the same error twice, and before calling a task done.
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

↳ https://t.co/bsYb2K5H9G

save it, you'll use this every single day.

celebrity.full_text_en:
We're sharing new data on how AI is changing research at OpenAI.

We find researchers' AI use continues to rise exponentially, and agents are completing longer tasks, but human involvement remains central in research. Researchers are also spending more time on safety and alignment, with human effort in these areas growing faster than in any other individual research area.

This report aims to increase transparency around research acceleration and inform the governance of increasingly capable AI. We believe that AI labs should be required to track and publicly report indicators of recursive self-improvement (RSI): the process by which AI accelerates the development of future AI systems. 

Our hope is that this expanded report will help sustain and advance shared measurement norms across the industry.

celebrity.full_text_en:
Akamai, a $12B company, built a SECOND version of its website that only AI agents could see.

its AI search visibility increased 364%, while citations jumped 85%.

here's the genius AEO system behind it:

/1 They realized AI wasn't reading their website the same way humans did

-> Akamai operates a massive website covering cybersecurity, cloud computing, and developer infrastructure.

-> but its content wasn't consistently appearing when people asked AI about the products it offered.

-> their team believed part of the problem was how AI agents were accessing and interpreting those pages.

/2 So they built TWO versions of the same website

-> when a normal person visited Akamai, they saw the regular website, with its design, navigation, and interactive elements.

-> but when a supported AI agent requested a page, Akamai's system delivered a different, simplified version.

-> same URL, same underlying product information, but without the extra code, menus, and other elements AI didn't need.

/3 They made it work automatically through their CDN

-> Akamai used its edge infrastructure to identify incoming AI traffic before the requests reached its website.

-> detected AI agents were routed through Scrunch's Agent Experience Platform, which delivered simpler HTML versions of Akamai's existing content.

-> unlike llms.txt (which major AI search engines don't reliably read), this approach delivers optimized content directly when supported AI agents request a page.

-> they didn't have to redesign their public website or manually rewrite every page.

/4 They removed unnecessary code from the pages AI received

-> modern websites contain a lot more than the information visitors actually need: JavaScript, navigation, interactive elements, and other code.

-> Scrunch produced machine-readable versions using Akamai's existing product pages and documentation.

-> the goal was to make the information easier for AI to retrieve and understand, without changing what human visitors saw.

/5 They didn't roll it out across the entire website immediately

-> the first test focused on pages related to Akamai's Inference Cloud offering.

-> they measured how these pages appeared across selected AI prompts before optimization.

-> then they compared pages receiving the optimized treatment against pages that weren't.

/6 The first results were pretty significant

-> optimized pages received 85% more total AI citations.

-> they were cited across 38% more unique prompts.

-> brand visibility for questions that DIDN'T mention Akamai by name increased 364%.

-> in ChatGPT, Akamai's brand presence against competitors improved 133%.

and this last point is especially important.

people weren't just asking "what is Akamai?" and getting Akamai's website back.

the company started appearing more often when buyers asked general questions about the problems its products solve.

/7 The company decided to expand the system

-> after the initial test, Akamai began rolling the approach out across more of its website.

-> it also turned the technology into a commercial product called AI Brand Presence.

-> the same infrastructure it uses to manage web traffic could now detect AI agents, change how they receive content, and measure the results.

Akamai essentially built a system where humans and AI receive different versions of the same underlying website information.

and in its initial test, that was associated with a 364% improvement in visibility for searches where people weren't even mentioning the brand.

人们不只是问“Akamai 是什么？”并恢复 Akamai 的网站。

celebrity.full_text_en:
I’ve watched plenty of AI agent demos that looked amazing. I wouldn’t trust any of them with my wallet.

That gap is what i keep coming back to. Imagine actually hiring an agent today, and count how many things could go wrong.

You can’t tell if it’s real. The name, bio, and “past work” can all be copied. A bad agent can disappear and return under a new name with a clean record.

You can’t check if it can do the job. There’s no history, just a pitch.

Payment is awkward either way. Pay first and you’re hoping. Pay after and the agent is hoping.

Nobody verifies the work. “Done” is just a word, and if you disagree, there’s no one to ask.

And there’s no record afterward. The next client walks into the same mess.

That’s fine for a demo. It breaks the moment agents work for money, and especially when agents start hiring other agents, because no human is there to catch the mistakes.

So i don’t see identity, reputation, and escrow as nice extras. They’re the minimum for an agent economy to exist at all. Humans built whole industries around them, and agents will need the same.

@termix_ai is building this layer. What I’ll be watching is whether it holds up under real jobs.

What’s the one thing an agent would need to show you before you’d let it handle real money?
celebrity.full_text_zh:
我看过很多看起来很棒的人工智能代理演示。我不会相信他们中的任何一个人会用我的钱包。

这个差距是我不断回想起的。想象一下今天实际雇用一名代理人，并计算一下有多少事情可能会出错。

你无法判断它是否真实。姓名、简历和“过去的工作”都可以复制。不良代理人可能会消失，然后以新的名字和干净的记录重新出现。

你无法检查它是否能完成这项工作。没有历史，只有一个球场。

无论哪种方式付款都很尴尬。先付款，你就满怀希望了。付款后，代理希望。

没有人验证工作。 “完成”只是一个词，如果你不同意，也没有人可以问。

而且之后就没有任何记录了。下一个客户也陷入了同样的困境。

对于演示来说这很好。它打破了代理人为金钱而工作的那一刻，尤其是当代理人开始雇用其他代理人时，因为没有人可以发现错误。

所以我不认为身份、声誉和托管是额外的好处。它们是代理经济存在的最低限度。人类围绕它们建立了整个行业，代理商也需要同样的东西。

@termix_ai 正在构建这一层。我将关注的是它是否适用于实际工作。

在您允许代理处理真实资金之前，代理需要向您展示什么？

celebrity.full_text_en:
My friend Laura has 56 days to find a job or leave the US.

Last Friday her company  NextSense furloughed the whole team. Laura is on an H1-B, which requires her to be paid while employed so her role was terminated and the 60 day clock started.

She's a biomedical engineer with a PhD in neuroscience. She builds ML for sleep and time-series signals like EEG/EMG and she has built wearable AI models in production.

She's looking for research scientist roles in the Bay Area.

If you're hiring in health tech or wearables, DM me and I'll intro you. @ycombinator founders: if you need a founding ML or research hire, she's it. Her H-1B transfers so no lottery needed.

And if you're not hiring, a repost might reach the person who is 🙏

https://t.co/9cJH8nmpiN
celebrity.full_text_zh:
我的朋友劳拉有 56 天的时间来找到工作或离开美国。

上周五，她的公司 NextSense 让整个团队休假。 Laura 持有 H1-B 签证，这要求她在工作期间领取工资，因此她的角色被终止，60 天的期限开始。

她是一名生物医学工程师，拥有神经科学博士学位。她为睡眠和脑电图/肌电图等时间序列信号构建了机器学习，并在生产中构建了可穿戴人工智能模型。

她正在湾区寻找研究科学家的职位。

如果您正在招聘健康技术或可穿戴设备领域的人才，请私信我，我会介绍您。 @ycombinator 创始人：如果你需要一名创始机器学习或研究人员，她就是你的选择。她的 H-1B 转让因此不需要抽签。

如果您不雇用，转发可能会到达正在雇用的人 🙏

prompts.title_en: Production-Grade Fullstack .cursorrules Template for Cursor & Windsurf
prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

2. 核心壁垒审计：其商业模式是否具备真正的防御性护城河（技术排他性、网络效应、沉没迁移成本还是数据飞轮）？
3. 单元经济模型（Unit Economics）：拆解 LTV/CAC、毛利率天花板与算力边际成本衰减曲线；
4. 风险清单：列出可能导致该赛道 3 年内崩溃的 3 个致命黑天鹅。

prompts.prompt_content_zh:

- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；

3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。

林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

"""

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Imagine having an AI Agent that can do more than answer questions.

With @meetmotes, the idea is to connect each Genesis NFT to a dedicated Agent and Smart Account, giving it a defined environment to work within.

But what does user control actually look like?

Imagine funding an Agent with 1,000 USDC to manage an approved list of DeFi assets.

You could set:
→ Maximum 10% per trade
→ A daily spending cap of 300 USDC
→ Slippage limit of 0.5%
→ Borrowing disabled
→ Pause new trades if the account value falls to 850 USDC

The Agent can research and propose actions, but transactions must pass the account's policy checks before execution.

That's the important distinction: AI can make decisions, but permissions should determine what it is allowed to do.

Motes' documentation describes this architecture, including policy enforcement, execution logs, pause controls and permission revocation.

What I still want to see is the evidence in practice:

→ Verified smart-account contracts and independent security reviews
→ Onchain records showing limits enforced on every transaction
→ Execution logs covering successful, rejected and failed actions
→ A tested pause and revocation process

The concept behind $MOTES is interesting, but reliable execution and genuine owner control need to be demonstrated, not just promised.

More research to come.

viral_posts.full_text_en:
The New York Times just ran Anthropic's best ad of the IPO. They call it a profile. It reads like a prospectus. The author left out who funded her reporting.

Another classic Anthropic puff piece. Receipts below.

On the surface, her pre-IPO profile of Anthropic in the New York Times lands a few soft, harmless jabs. Strip away the Silicon Valley jargon, though, and every "critique" turns into a high-end sales pitch aimed straight at "Americans' retirement portfolios." That's you.

Here are the receipts she printed, and the one she hid.

1. The "reluctant hero" trick.

After paragraphs of employees agonizing over how to "slow down A.I.," the piece admits Anthropic's #1 priority with IPO cash is buying massive compute to reach "recursive self-improvement" (AI building uncontrollable AI) before OpenAI and China.

Meanwhile, it warns about mass layoffs while being the leading seller of the AI agents that "threaten to replace white-collar workers."

It sells the flood and the sandbags.

2. The $70 billion fund, and the fine print.

The company is putting 5% of a $1.4T company ($70 billion) into a "Public Benefit Fund" for donations of its choosing. Its employees are pledging their stock to charity too.

Read her order: animal welfare, global health, AI safety. Then, last: "Many have begun giving big to political campaigns."

Charity on the label. Politics in the fine print.

Tucked between the "ascetic monk" anecdotes is the real pitch: insiders aren't selling, Claude Code "reinvented" coding, and revenue passed OpenAI.

That isn't a profile. That's a prospectus with a byline.

3. The monopoly free pass.

Anthropic is lobbying Congress for an antitrust exemption (a legal cartel), pre-empting state AI laws, and talking about becoming "more powerful than the government."

A five-tier stock structure: you buy the shares, they keep the vote.

Count the named critics in the entire piece: zero.

Even after citing examples of Claude "only pretending to follow its instructions," how does Sun let it off the hook? One magic sentence:

"I do not doubt these good intentions."

Compare how she treats regular Americans. In August, she toured the Midwest towns fighting AI data centers on their land, then filed their anger under: "'AI populism' is more about populism than about AI."

A Wisconsin town fights a data center: populism.
A trillion-dollar AI lab sells its IPO: good intentions.

The neighbors get diagnosed. The billionaires get believed.

4. The missing receipt.

The biggest conflict isn't in Anthropic's prospectus. It's in the byline.

The money: Sun's August data-center story ends: "This story was supported by a grant from the Tarbell Center for AI Journalism." Tarbell is bankrolled by Coefficient Giving, the foundation of Anthropic early investor Dustin Moskovitz.

The overlap: She wrote that her D.C. party overlapped with the Coefficient Giving team retreat: "The lines got blurry—I think my group was the intersection of both."

Her words. Not mine.

5. The hypocrisy.

On 80,000 Hours, she set the rule: "I don't think that you can do especially credible either journalistic work or policy advocacy work if you are employed by a lab: you are going to be seen as a shill. You are correctly seen as a shill."

Same show, when the money came from the lab's investors instead of the lab, she called that a witch hunt: they're "going after all the Tarbell fellows and saying these people are just Anthropic shills."

Lab paycheck: shill. Lab investor's grant: witch hunt.

Then she took a Tarbell grant herself. Then she wrote Anthropic's IPO profile in the New York Times. Then she left out the disclosure.

Her rule. Her money. Her silence.

In August, she could type the disclosure. In November, on the eve of Anthropic's IPO, she left it out.

So admit it.

You took money from Anthropic's investor network. Admit it.
You were in the room with the funders. Your words. Admit it.
You wrote their sales pitch on the eve of their IPO. Admit it.
You left out the one sentence you already know how to type.

Regular Americans report every dollar to the IRS. 
You couldn't spare your readers one sentence.

By her own standard, what is she?

《纽约时报》刚刚刊登了 Anthropic 首次公开募股的最佳广告。他们称之为个人资料。它读起来就像招股说明书。作者没有提及谁资助了她的报道。

从表面上看，她在《纽约时报》上对 Anthropic 进行首次公开​​募股前的介绍，受到了一些温和、无害的攻击。不过，抛开硅谷的行话，每一次“批评”都会变成直接针对“美国人的退休投资组合”的高端推销。那就是你。

这是她打印的收据和她藏起来的收据。

1.“英雄不甘”的伎俩。

在一段段员工苦苦思索如何“放慢人工智能速度”之后，这篇文章承认，Anthropic 在 IPO 现金方面的第一要务是购买大量计算资源，以在 OpenAI 和 China 之前实现“递归自我改进”（人工智能构建无法控制的人工智能）。

与此同时，该公司警告说，在成为“威胁要取代白领工人”的人工智能代理的主要销售商的同时，该公司可能会出现大规模裁员。

它出售洪水和沙袋。

2. 700 亿美元的基金和细则。

该公司将一家价值 1.4T 美元的公司（700 亿美元）的 5% 投入“公共福利基金”，用于其选择的捐赠。它的员工也将他们的股票捐献给慈善机构。

阅读她的命令：动物福利、全球健康、人工智能安全。然后，最后：“许多人已经开始大力支持政治运动。”

标签上的慈善。精美印刷中的政治。

在“苦行僧”轶事之间隐藏着真正的卖点：内部人士不出售，Claude Code“重新发明”了编码，收入超过了 OpenAI。

Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Thursday! A new morning, a fresh cup of coffee, and another interesting development in the AI agent space.

Something I've been paying attention to with @termix_ai is how it approaches the onboarding problem.

Building an AI agent is one thing. Giving that agent access to real opportunities and letting it participate in an economy is another challenge.

TermiX is working to make this connection simpler through its Agent Skills.

Instead of requiring developers to build an entirely new agent from scratch, they can connect existing AI agents to TermiX and let them interact with https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3.

Once connected, agents can discover services, respond to opportunities, take jobs, and participate in the on-chain settlement process.

I think this matters because adoption often depends on how easily existing tools can become part of a new ecosystem.

If developers can bring the agents they already use into a shared marketplace, TermiX doesn't have to rely only on people creating new agents specifically for its platform.

Of course, easier access also brings new responsibilities. Permissions, wallet security, transaction limits, and human oversight remain important when agents are allowed to act on our behalf.

For me, the interesting question is no longer just how smart an AI agent can become.

It's how easily that agent can connect to other services, find useful work, and create real value.

That's an important direction for the agent economy, and one worth watching as TermiX continues to evolve.

Have a productive Thursday, everyone! 🚀

朋友们早上好！ ☀️☕

星期四快乐！新的早晨，一杯新鲜的咖啡，以及人工智能代理领域的另一个有趣的发展。

我一直关注 @termix_ai 的是它如何解决入职问题。

构建人工智能代理是一回事。让代理人获得真正的机会并让其参与经济是另一个挑战。

TermiX 正在努力通过其代理技能来简化这种连接。

他们无需要求开发人员从头开始构建全新的代理，而是可以将现有的 AI 代理连接到 TermiX，并让它们与 进行交互。

连接后，代理可以发现服务、响应机会、接受工作并参与链上结算流程。

我认为这很重要，因为采用通常取决于现有工具成为新生态系统一部分的容易程度。

如果开发人员可以将他们已经使用的代理引入共享市场，TermiX 就不必仅仅依靠人们专门为其平台创建新代理。

当然，更便捷的访问也带来了新的责任。当允许代理代表我们行事时，权限、钱包安全、交易限制和人工监督仍然很重要。

对我来说，有趣的问题不再只是人工智能代理能变得多聪明。

这是代理可以多么轻松地连接到其他服务、找到有用的工作并创造真正的价值。

这是代理经济的一个重要方向，随着 TermiX 的不断发展，值得关注。

大家周四过得充实！ 🚀

当然，更便捷的访问也带来了新的责任。当允许代理代表我们行事时，权限、钱包安全、交易限制和人工监督仍然很重要。

对我来说，有趣的问题不再只是人工智能代理能变得多聪明。

这是代理可以多么轻松地连接到其他服务、找到有用的工作并创造真正的价值。

这是代理经济的一个重要方向，随着 TermiX 的不断发展，值得关注。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 together, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Opus-level judgment on every big call, without paying Opus rates for every routine turn.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes the code
→ Haiku 5.5 explores files and docs in parallel
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls
→ you stop spending Opus on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku explores. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and edits code
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5
> docs pulls the API reference on Haiku 5.5
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reads the whole transcript when consulted
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three read-only Haiku 5.5 subagents: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), docs (pulls the API reference).
3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before locking a plan, after the same error twice, and before calling a task done.
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

↳ https://t.co/bsYb2K5H9G

save it, you'll use this every single day.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
这是真正的黄金

Anthropic 刚刚分享了 Claude Code 的最佳技巧之一。

想法：一起运行 Sonnet、Haiku 和 Opus 5.5，每个都只做它最擅长的工作。

对每个重大跟注进行 Opus 级别的判断，无需为每个例行回合支付 Opus 费率。

你只需像这样启动 Claude Code：

克劳德——模型十四行诗——顾问作品

这是分裂：

→ Sonnet 5.5 运行会话并编写代码
→ Haiku 5.5 并行探索文件和文档
→ Opus 5.5 作为重大呼叫的顾问随时待命
→ 您停止将 Opus 花在不需要的工作上

Opus 只在三个时刻介入：

→ 计划锁定之前
→ 当同样的错误出现两次时
→ 在完成之前

十四行诗构建。俳句探索。作品评论。

JEV工程是相同的向下一层：不需要思考者（哪个文件，哪个工具，重试或停止）的分叉在几毫秒内进入JEV，而大模型只能看到分裂的分叉

完整的树
> Sonnet 5.5 运行主会话并编辑代码
> 搜索映射 Haiku 5.5 上的存储库
> grep 查找 Haiku 5.5 上的调用站点
> 文档拉取 Haiku 5.5 上的 API 参考
> Opus 5.5 作为顾问随时待命，在咨询时阅读整个记录
> JEV 在几毫秒内完成微分叉路线

将树和此提示粘贴到 Claude Code 中 ↓

“围绕这棵树重建我的 Claude Code 设置：
1. 以 Opus 5.5 作为顾问，在 Sonnet 5.5 上运行主要会话。
2. 创建三个只读 Haiku 5.5 子代理：search（映射存储库）、grep（查找调用站点）、docs（提取 API 参考）。
3. 在 CLAUDE.md 中添加一条规则：在锁定计划之前、两次出现相同错误之后以及在调用任务完成之前咨询顾问。
4. 通过 JEV 路由快速确定性分叉（工具选择、路径选择、重试）。
首先将每个更改显示为差异。在我说走之前不能进行任何编辑。”

↳

viral_posts.full_text_en:
We're sharing new data on how AI is changing research at OpenAI.

We find researchers' AI use continues to rise exponentially, and agents are completing longer tasks, but human involvement remains central in research. Researchers are also spending more time on safety and alignment, with human effort in these areas growing faster than in any other individual research area.

This report aims to increase transparency around research acceleration and inform the governance of increasingly capable AI. We believe that AI labs should be required to track and publicly report indicators of recursive self-improvement (RSI): the process by which AI accelerates the development of future AI systems. 

Our hope is that this expanded report will help sustain and advance shared measurement norms across the industry.

https://t.co/xyGPcCkPCK
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
我们正在 OpenAI 上分享有关人工智能如何改变研究的新数据。

我们发现研究人员对人工智能的使用持续呈指数级增长，智能体正在完成更长的任务，但人类的参与仍然是研究的核心。研究人员也在安全和协调上花费了更多的时间，人类在这些领域的努力比任何其他单独的研究领域增长得更快。

本报告旨在提高研究加速的透明度，并为日益强大的人工智能的治理提供信息。我们认为，应该要求人工智能实验室跟踪并公开报告递归自我改进（RSI）指标：人工智能加速未来人工智能系统开发的过程。

我们希望这份扩展报告将有助于维持和推进整个行业的共享衡量规范。
